ALTERNATIVES
The proposed legislation provides for the Secretary of Commerce to assume partial jurisdiction for some marine species including seals, whales, oceanic fishes, certain anadromous fishes, marine mollusks and crustaceans. An alternative to the proposed action would be to continue sole administration of the endangered species program by the Interior, the department charged with primary responsibility for protection of the Nation's wildlife resources.
THE FLORIDA AUDUBON SOCIETY CONSIDERS THIS ALTERNATIVE THE MOST IMPORTANT COMMENT IN THE DRAFT IMPACT STATEMENT. THE DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE HAS NO BUSINESS REGULATING THE TAKING OF ENDANGERED SPECIES SUCH AS THE BLUE WHALE, SEA OTTER, ETC. WHEN THE PHILOSOPHY OF THE DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE (N.O.A.A.) IS "THE MAXIMUM SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION OF FISH AND FISHERY PRODUCTS."
In conclusion, the Florida Audubon Society desires to see the "endangered species list" greatly expanded. The burden of proving that the species is not endangered should be placed in the hands of the people who would exploit wildlife.
In addition, the national wildlife refuges should be closed to hunting. We do not consider an area a "refuge" where hunting is allowed. In Florida, the only "inviolate refuges" for wildlife are the Audubon and Nature Conservancy sanctuaries. We fail to see State or Federal interest in the establishment of inviolate wildlife sanctuaries.
